topic: This week in AI: the top 5 stories you need to know
post:
This week, AI was all about one word: control. 🎛️
Here are the top 5 stories you need to know.

1️⃣ Schools get the switch
Google announced that K-12 student accounts will have Gemini and Search off until a school admin turns them on. Reports say the details are still coming.

2️⃣ AI flunked the voter guide test
The Washington Post and NPR found chatbots giving wrong election info, from made-up races to wrong registration deadlines.

3️⃣ Siri opens up
Apple opened Siri AI to app developers in the iOS 27.3 beta, so apps can bring their content and actions into Siri.

4️⃣ A kill switch for AI agents
CrowdStrike launched an "AI Kill Switch" to cut off agents that go rogue, and announced plans to buy Fiddler AI and Dreadnode. 🛑

5️⃣ AI customer service consolidates
Five9 agreed to buy Level AI for about $325 million in cash.

Why it matters:
AI is moving into schools, phones and the workplace. The big question is no longer "can it do this?" but "who decides when it's on, and how do we stop it?" ⚖️

Practical takeaway:
For every AI tool you use at work, know where its off switch is. 🔍

Which story matters most to you? 👇

Follow for daily AI news you can actually use.
